dropped: Thomson: UK retailer price found (Currys Business, NEO10) was an anomalous clearance/typo-range (£19.15) with no verifiable exact configuration behind it; no honest single-SKU price could be confirmed.
Star Labs: every published figure for StarBook Horizon/Horizon Plus/Ultra is a 'from' price for a configurable base build; excluded because the brief disallows starting-at prices.
Tuxedo Computers: InfinityBook Pro/Max prices found were all 'starts at' figures for a configurable build; excluded for the same reason as Star Labs.
Digital Storm: only named-model price points (Vanquish II $699, Eclipse $699, Apollo $1,495, etc.) were found with no CPU/RAM/storage tied to a specific one of those names in the same source.
Infinix: INBook Air Pro Plus price ($599) came only from a cross-market aggregator (ectgadget) with no CPU/RAM/storage for that exact SKU; dropped rather than guess specs.

Shuttle, Acemagic: Acemagic prices found were all discount-code or flash-sale prices stacked on an unstated regular price (e.g. 'discounted to $575, or $546 with code'), which the brief's honesty rule on sale/regular pairs doesn't cleanly fit; Shuttle yielded no single priced SKU at all.
reMarkable: the Paper Pro is an E Ink writing tablet with no conventional CPU/RAM/storage specification published, so it does not fit this catalog's required fields honestly.

Tecno, Avita India-market lines, Toshiba-branded (Dynabook-made) models, Getac, Durabook, Pine64, Kamrui, Bmax, Ninkear, Falcon Northwest, Xidax: considered but no single retailer listing tying one exact configuration to one exact regular price was found in the time available.
